headline: Approved a regulation banning sale and distribution of synthetic cannabinoids, kratom products, and unregulated novel intoxicating products, effective September 1, 2026.
summary: A public hearing was held on the regulation, and several residents spoke in support of it. The regulation bans the manufacture, sale, and distribution of synthetic cannabinoids, kratom products, and unregulated novel intoxicating products. Members also rescinded the former regulation on synthetic cannabinoids.
decisions: Approved the June 9, 2026 meeting minutes by a vote of 3 to 0.

Approved the regulation prohibiting the manufacture, sale and distribution of synthetically derived cannabinoids, Kratom products, and unregulated intoxicating products, effective September 1, 2026, by a vote of 4 to 0.
Rescinded former Regulation #34 on synthetic cannabinoids by a vote of 4 to 0, as it would be redundant to the amended regulation effective September 1, 2026.

7:02pm 
 
J. Schiller motioned to approve the minutes S. Lunde 2nd. All in favor. 
 
Motion passed by a vote of 3 to 0.  
 
The Board discussed taking the agenda out of order to address the proposed 
new regulation first.  
 
S. Lunde motioned to take the agenda out of order J. Schiller 2nd. All 
in favor. 
 
Motion passed by a vote of 3 to 0.  
 
 
The Board opened the public hearing regarding the updated Board of 
Health Regulation #34 regulation prohibiting the manufacturing, sale, and 
distribution of synthetically derived cannabinoids, kratom products, and 
unregulated novel intoxicating products.  Board member Dee Elias arrived 
as the public hearing began.   
J. Redford provided the Board with an overview of the revised regulation.  
She explained that the draft regulation the Board agreed upon included 
synthetically derived cannabinoids, kratom products, and unregulated novel 
intoxicating products.  She explained that the regulation received legal 
review from the Board of Health technical assistance provider MA 
Association of Health Boards and the City Solicitor’s office.  The City 
Solicitor’s office made some amendments that were incorporated into the 
final regulation. 
J. Schiller asked if someone could grow a Kratom plant under this 
regulation.  It was explained that they could because the Board was not 
criminalizing Kratom.  The Boad is prohibiting the sale and distribution of 
these products. 
S. Moore asked if all the City Solicitor’s concerns have been addressed. D. 
Greenbaum explained that he had some minor edits that he incorporated 
into the regulation before the Board.
2 | P a g e 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
S. Moore stated she was struck by the messages the Board received in 
support of the ban.  
D. Greenbaum stated that it would be important to have those emails 
officially entered into the record. He explained that the Board received 3 
emails from who were strongly in support of the regulation. They were 
from Holly Trouville, Shannon Mandeville, and Dan Gibbs.   
S. Moore read the three emails into the record, and all are on file.  
D. Greenbaum advised the Board that the email provided by Mr. Gibbs did 
not contain any of the attachments he mentioned in his email.  He also 
informed the Board that he had been provided with an article from Stars 
and Strips magazine from the Pentagon prohibiting the use of the drug.  
J. Schiller asked if we received any written testimony against it banning the 
regulation?  D. Greenbaum explained that we did not receive any written 
testimony against the regulation. 
S. Lunde stated that the Board added other unregulated novel and 
intoxicating products.  He feels that is the main thing, we should not be 
allowing things to be sold to children that we do not know what they are. 
He stated, without regulation he thinks there is no chance for the Board to 
know that there is not some illicit substance in any of these bags because of 
where they're coming from. 
Susan Eppard testified that she would like the Board to ban all forms of 
kratom.  Her son Matthew died at 22 years old from full-leaf all-natural 
kratom Powder. He died in 2021 before there were any semi-synthetics or 
synthetic kratoms available.  It caused him to have a seizure, go into 
cardiac arrest and die instantly on his kitchen floor.  His toxicology and 
autopsy showed he had no underlying health conditions.  He had no 
prescription drugs, no street drugs, and no alcohol in his system.  He was 
an otherwise perfectly healthy 22-year-old who should have lived out his 
entire life. She implored the Board to ban all forms of kratom.  
S. Moore thanked Ms. Eppard for her testimony and on behalf of the Board 
gave her condolences on the loss of her son. 
Holly Trouville advised the Board that Tisbury on Matha's Vineyard band 
Kratom at 4 o’clock today.  She stated that the neighboring community of 
Beverly has a hearing to ban it tomorrow, and Peabody has a hearing 
coming up.  Melrose Stoneham and other areas have already banned it as 
well.  She implored the Board to be all forms of Kratom.  She added there 
is no way to test this to know what it really is.  She does not think people 
should be determining their own doses, especially when most people doing 
it are recovering addicts that they say have helped them get off other drugs.  
She does not think that is wise for anybody to be determining their own 
dosage of something that isn't regulated.  She stated that you will hear a lot 
of people say the FDA just wants to ban 70H, but you go on their website 
they are not regulating it.  If you look on the back of those bags that you 
buy in any of your stores, it says only for a botanical specimen, which 
means not for human consumption.  The FDA could approve Kratom for 
human consumption, and it has not.  That should be very telling. 
S. Moore stated appreciated hearing from people about their experiences 
and the losses that people experienced.  She reiterated that the Board 
acknowledged there could be some benefit to natural Kratom, she felt there 
was no way to know what was in anything being sold. The Board was not 
criminalizing the use of Kratom.  People can certainly still access it. 
But as a Board of Health, it is important for us to look out for public health

D. Elias inquired that while reviewing the email, it says that the Board 
cannot issue the $1,000 fine directly and asked if this was in the final draft 
of the regulation. 
D. Greenbaum explained that this was clarified by the technical assistance 
provider, the MA Association of Health Boards.  Under MGL Chapter 111. 
Section 31, Boards of Health do have the authority to issue fines of $1,000 
per offense.  That information was provided to the City Solicitor, and he 
agreed that was appropriate to include it in the regulation. 
 
S. Lunde motioned to approve the Salem Board of Health regulation 
prohibiting the manufacture, sale and distribution of synthetically 
derived cannabinoids, Kratom products, and unregulated intoxicating 
products.  Effective September 1st, 2026.  J. Schiller 2nd. All in favor. 
 
Motion passed by a vote of 4 to 0.  
 
 
J. Schiller motioned rescind the former Board of Health regulations 
#34 that prohibited the manufacture, sale, and distribution of synthetic 
cannabinoids, as it would be redundant to the amended regulation 
effective September 1, 2026.  D. Elias 2nd. All in favor. 
 
Motion passed by a vote of 4 to 0.  
 
 
Discussion took place regarding how businesses would be notified about 
this new regulation.  D. Greenbaum stated that a notice would go out to all 
convenience stores where these products are believed to be sold.  Staff 
would notify any business after September 1st where these products were 
found of the regulations.  Discussions also took place regarding additional 
messaging on social media and the website. 
 
D. Greenbaum advised the Board that the Beverly-Salem Water Supply 
Board had submitted a permit request to temporarily suspend the 
application of fluoride for 60 days.  He wanted the Board to be aware of 
this submittal.  He advised the Board that the administrative report was also 
available for review.  This outlines all the financial information for the 
department. 
He advised the Board that the City of Salem has been named in a federal 
lawsuit regarding the FDA marketing granting order letter that was sent in 
May with an enforcement date of July 1, 2026.  The suit includes 16 
communities, the Commissioner of Public Health, and MA DPH.  The suit 
basically states that the Boards of Health have exceed their authority to take 
this action.  We are coordinating with the Department of Public Health to 
determine how this is going to proceed.  The lawsuit claims that we are 
enforcing federal law.  We are not enforcing federal law.  We are requiring 
our permit holders to comply with federal law as a requirement of their 
tobacco permit. 
J. Redford added that the suit includes 16 total communities and of those 
communities 5 are within our collaborative.

on July 1st.  He is working with the City Solicitor’s office to draft some
